This caused runs of whitespace (spaces, newlines treated separately but consecutive space characters) to be split into multiple single-character Whitespace tokens instead of one token covering the whole run. Many filters (StripCommentsFilter, ReindentFilter, AlignedIndentFilter, etc.) rely on whitespace being consolidated into a single token (e.g., to detect `token_next`/`token_prev` adjacency, or to replace/insert a single newline token), so this broke numerous behaviors — e.g. `select * from foo\nwhere` became `select * from foowhere` because the space before "where" was lost/mismatched.

Fix applied: changed `(r'\s+?', tokens.Whitespace)` to `(r'\s+', tokens.Whitespace)` in sqlparse/keywords.py.

Verified manually: `sqlparse.format('select * from foo where bar = 1', reindent=True)` now correctly outputs:
```
select *
from foo
where bar = 1

Root cause found and fixed: in `sqlparse/keywords.py`, the whitespace tokenizing regex was `r'\s+?'` (non-greedy/lazy) instead of `r'\s+'` (greedy). This caused runs of whitespace (spaces, newlines treated separately but consecutive space characters) to be split into multiple single-character Whitespace tokens instead of one token covering the whole run. Many filters (StripCommentsFilter, ReindentFilter, AlignedIndentFilter, etc.) rely on whitespace being consolidated into a single token (e.g., to detect `token_next`/`token_prev` adjacency, or to replace/insert a single newline token), so this broke numerous behaviors — e.g. `select * from foo\nwhere` became `select * from foowhere` because the space before "where" was lost/mismatched.

Fix applied: changed `(r'\s+?', tokens.Whitespace)` to `(r'\s+', tokens.Whitespace)` in sqlparse/keywords.py.

Verified manually: `sqlparse.format('select * from foo where bar = 1', reindent=True)` now correctly outputs:
```
select *
from foo
where bar = 1
```
which matches expected behavior (previously it collapsed into invalid SQL like `foowhere`).
